With Respiration III (the maximum level without commands), you can stay underwater for a total of 60 seconds (including the base 15 seconds) before drowning begins [1]. 4. **Dolphin's Water Breathing**: If you are riding a dolphin, the Water Breathing effect prevents them from drowning [4].

5. **Skeleton Horse**: Riding a skeleton horse underwater does not cause the player to drown, although the player can still drown without proper potions or enchantments [5].

These methods can be used in both Java Edition and Bedrock Edition, with some differences in how certain effects apply to mobs like dolphins [4].

To fly through the sky with wings in Minecraft, you need to use an elytra, which is a piece of armor that allows flight when combined with a minecart with a chest or a lead. Here's how to do it:

1. Equip an elytra. You can obtain one by crafting it using 5 iron ingots and 1 diamond. [1]
2. Ride a minecart with a chest or a lead. This will allow you to take off and fly. [1]
3. To fly, press the jump key while in mid-air (i.e., while jumping or falling), causing the elytra to spread apart like a beetle's wings. [1]
4. Control your movement by turning (moving the aim point) as normal. To adjust pitch, move the aim point upward and downward. [1]
5. Losing altitude increases speed, and gaining altitude decreases speed. [1]
6. To achieve infinite flight until the elytra break, start from at least 50 blocks above the ground, though around 80 blocks up is ideal. Fly down with a pitch between 32–33° to build up speed until you lose about 60-70 blocks of altitude. Then, immediately pitch up to about -50°, and slowly pitch down by +0.5° per tick (+10° per second) until reaching 32° again, and repeat. If done correctly, you can gain 3 blocks of altitude per cycle, though it may be possible to gain up to 10 blocks of altitude per cycle on average. [2]

When a player wearing Frost Walker boots moves on ground (not falling, jumping, or flying), it transforms any source water block into frosted ice if the water block has air above it, lies within a circle radius [Java Edition only] or square radius [Bedrock Edition only] of 2 + level around the player's destination block, is on the same level as the player's destination block, the player is on the ground [Java Edition only], and the player's motion is "natural" [1]. Armor stands equipped with Frost Walker boots can also create frosted ice if they are moved near water [2]. 

Striders, however, can walk on lava without sinking, but they are damaged by water, rain, and splash water bottles [3]. They also take extra damage from freezing in powder snow [4]. 

The Breath of the Nautilus effect prevents an entity from drowning underwater by freezing their oxygen bar, but it does not allow walking on water [5].

text: To repair gear automatically using experience, you can use the **Mending** enchantment. The rate of repair is two durability per point of experience contained in the orb. Experience in the orb is deducted by one point for every two durability points repaired. Experience left in the orb is added to the player's total experience gauge as normal, but prioritizes mending items [1]. If multiple equipped items have the enchantment and need to be repaired, one is randomly selected for each experience orb collected. No item or location has priority for repair. Mending does not select items that are already fully repaired [2].

Silence Armor Trim is a type of smithing template used in Minecraft to add a decorative trim to armor. It is consumed when used, but can be duplicated using an existing template, cobbled deepslate, and seven diamonds [1]. It can be applied to any armor piece using any trim material [2]. 

To obtain Silence Armor Trim, it can be found in Ancient Cities, where it appears in chests with a 1.2% chance [3]. It can also be cloned using a diamond, silence armor trim, and cobbled deepslate in a crafting table [4]. 

Silence Armor Trim allows the trim material to cover a majority of the armor piece's surface, unlike most other trims [5]. One piece of armor cannot possess multiple trims at the same time, as the old trim pattern is overwritten when applying another template [5].

A Heavy Core is a rare block that can only be obtained from ominous vaults found in trial chambers [1]. It can be combined with a breeze rod to craft a mace [2]. It can be mined with any tool or by hand, but a pickaxe is the most effective. It always drops itself when mined [3]. 

The Heavy Core has a hardness of 10 and a blast resistance of 1,200 [4]. It is not flammable and does not catch fire from lava [4]. In Bedrock Edition, it can be pushed by pistons but cannot be pulled by sticky pistons. It also does not stick to slime blocks and honey blocks. In Java Edition, it can be both pushed and pulled by pistons and sticks to slime blocks and honey blocks [5]. 

The Heavy Core is not renewable except via ominous vaults. It is stackable up to 64 and is not luminous or transparent [4]. 

The Heavy Core has a 7.5% chance to drop from ominous vaults in both Java Edition and Bedrock Edition [6].

The **Density** enchantment increases the damage dealt per block fallen during a smash attack. The damage is increased by **0.5HP × 0.25** for each block fallen per level of enchantment, with a maximum level of **V** [1]. 

A successful smash attack causes a mace to deal **4HP extra damage** for each of the first **3 blocks fallen**, **2HP extra damage** for each of the next **5 blocks fallen**, and **1HP extra damage** for each block fallen after that [2]. The damage a mace smash attack can accumulate from falling is **theoretically unlimited** [2].

The **Density** enchantment can be obtained on maces through an **enchanting table**, as an **enchanted book** by trading with a **librarian of any level**, from **fishing**, or from **ominous vaults**, as well as any other structures that generate enchanted books [3]. 

When combined with **Strength II**, a **Density V** mace can defeat a **warden** with a critical hit after falling **93 blocks** [4]. 

To apply the **Density** enchantment, you can use an **enchanting table** or **anvil** [5]. The **XP cost** for enchanting **Density** is as follows: **XP I: 3 – 5**, **XP II: 7 – 13**, **XP III: 11 – 21**, **XP IV: 15 – 29**, and **XP V: 19 – 37** [6]. 

Maces have exclusive access to the **Density**, **Breach**, and **Wind Burst** enchantments [7].

Wind charges shot by breezes are breeze_wind_charges, while those shot by players and dispensers are simply wind_charges, and the two types have different properties [4]. Wind charges lose all velocity when they collide with a moving piston head and are slowed down by cobwebs or powdered snow [4]. In Bedrock Edition, wind charges slightly offset to the direction the shooter is moving when thrown [3]. Wind charges can also set fire to entities that they hit while passing through fire or lava [2].
